Messages.Author: SirTemple
Messages.Body:
I think this is everyone who voted thus far.
It is 15-0 for making Concealed Weapon discaplineless.
Here are the reasons to support the change that we have advocated.

Given card text:
Concealed Weapon: "Equip this minion with a weapon card from your hand at the
begining of a round. Pay weapon's equip cost from blood poll, as normal. The
weapon cannot cost more than two pool or do more than 4 damage.

Disguised Weapon: "Equip this vampire with a weapon card from your hand. Only
usable at the beginning of a round. Pay weapon's cost from blood pool as
normal. AS ABOVE, BUT USABLE WHEN CHOOSING A STRIKE.

1. It is not logical to have two cards doing the same thing, especially when
one is a limited version of the other. For the same cost DW does what a
concealed weapon does, and possibly more. There is no reason to use a
Concealed weapon in the game when you can use Disguised Weapon.

2. Card text supports CW being discaplineless. DW specifies that it is usable
only by a vampire, while CW allows any minion to use it. Since only Vampires
may possess Obfuscate, it once again makes sence for DW to require it and CW to
be discaplineless.

3. Card format supports proposition. DW is set up with a basic and supperior
level like most discapline based cards. CW is set up like most discaplineless
cards, only one version, no superior.

4. Card concept supprts change. It is quite feasible to supprise an opponent
with a small concealed weapon. CW does this by limiting thae weapons cost and
damage. DW on the other hand is the use of a super-natural ability, and
therefore can produce any weapon.

5. Card picture supports this concept. The character on CW is simply pulling
a small gun out of his coat. He is not using any special tricks, simple
pulling out his concealed weapon.

Does anyone else have an additional reason before we submit the proposal?

Messages.Author: Lupus Australis
Messages.Body:
On 16 Mar 1998, SirTemple wrote:

> Does anyone else have an additional reason before we submit the proposal?

Yes.

All of the above is convincing as far as it goes. But the Powers That Be
were probably already aware of much, if not all, of it. Still, rather
than add to the already expanding list of errata, they chose to simply
discontinue the card as the redundant wallpaper it was (this decision
being based on your reason #1). Thus, Concealed Weapon was dropped from
the V:tES set to make room for some new Anti-Bleed cards.

That is why I assume they dropped the card instead of trying to salvage it
with errata: 1) they wanted to make room for the anti-bleed cards, 2)
they did not want to add to the errata lists, and most importantly 3) they
did not think a disciplineless version of DW was needed for the game.

If we want the Powers That Be to change their minds, we need to convince
them that they were wrong about reason #3. We need to convince them that
Concealed Weapon, if properly fixed, would improve and benefit the game.
If it were merely an issue of saving CW itself from being wallpaper, then
I would see no reason not to let it rot in wallpaper hell along with
the original "Chainsaw".

The proposed fix would not merely save CW from being wallpaper. It would
help save a whole host of other cards from being wallpaper too. It would
give both weapons and allies, both of which are horrendously underused, a
needed boost, adding to the balance, variety, and unpredictability of the
game. I think this is what needs to be emphasized. I need not elaborate
further, since my arguments along these lines were detailed in my original
post.

True, though why is that wrong? The "wasted time" of an equip action is
one of the reasons why equip actions are so rarely done, and weapons are
just not a part of combat, as I believe they were intended to be.

>You'd be foolish to ever consider an action to equip ever again.

Well, that's simply not true. I play with Nossies all the time, and we
certainly do take equip actions. We even occasionally take equip actions
with weapons. There is not always room in the deck for both the weapons
I want and the DWs to help bring them out. Or maybe my deck has only one
or two weapons in it. In that case, even if I do put in one or two DWs to
complement them, there is an excellent chance that I will not be lucky
enough to have both in my hand at the same time. I will either have my
hand jammed with 2 DWs, which I will be forced to discard, or with 2
weapons, obliging me to take an action to equip.

>I always felt that the Powers That Be changed CW over to Obfuscate when
>they realized there would be no real need for DW, and no
>"pseudo-equipping" advantage to the Obfuscate discipline, if CW were
>to be disciplineless.

I don't think the greater advantage of Obfuscate was meant to be
pseudo-equiping. It is the Brujah, not the Nossies or the Malkavians, who
were supposed to be the typical and most efficient weapon users,
especially as they have the Arms Dealers to help them to coordinate CW and
Weapon in their hand at the same time.

The advantage of the inferior version of DW over CW is no greater (and, I
would argue, no less) than that of Undead Strength over Lucky Blow. The
superior version of DW, however, I would argue gives a significant
advantage, especially if your minion is not the acting one, as your
opponent does not know when he strikes that you will be pulling out
Talbot's Chainsaw or Bomb.

I put a few Assault Rifles in my Nossie Blood Generator Deck once, and

thought we Weenie Voter Consanguinous Boon Callers were helpless.

>CW doesn't sufficiently limit exactly what weapons
>it allows minions without Obf to get without risk of a blocked action.

I would have preferred that Unique Weapons be excluded, but this because I
am just a little jealous of my Nossies' privileges, not because I think
it makes Weapon-based combat too powerful.

>Sorry, but I _like_ the fact that there's at least a shot of blocking
>someone from equipping with the Ivory Bow, even if its just a wistful
>thought, as my Nosferatu look on in abject horror ;-) That
>opportunity to block is gone once CW is disciplineless.

To a large extent it is, but why should it not be this way? Are you
really afraid that weapon-based combat will become TOO powerful? The
difficulty and time getting weapons into play is one of the major reasons
(along with their cost) they are not played at all.

> This would also speed up weenie gun decks, as there is no delay for
>the equip action. Another negative, IMHO.

The only thing wrong with Weenie Gun decks, that I can see, is Zip
Gun/DBR, but that is a separate issue. A disciplineless CW has not a
chance to be nearly as abusive as that combo.

Look, if weapon-based combat becomes a problem for you, heres what you can
do:

Shattering Blow: Destroys his stuff before he can use it.
Canine Horde: Destroys his stuff at long range before he can use it.
Fast Hands: Takes his weapon away from him (then you additional strike
and use it against him).
Peace Treaty: Forces Players with Weapons to pay again or burn them.
Immortal Grapple: Prevents opponent from using weapon strikes.
Blood Rage/Blood Fury: Prevents opponent from doing damage with weapons.

with weapon-based combat if it becomes a persistant nuisance.

them as DOTB is one of the most deadly and reliable of all weapon hosers.

: "pseudo-equipping" advantage to the Obfuscate discipline, if CW were
: to be disciplineless.

Hmmm. Well, you make some reasonable points here, but I have to take
issue with at least one of them: You suggest that the designers knowingly
changed CW to Obfuscate, so as to keep it from being disciplineless and
screwing up the game. But that implies stupidity on their part even
beyond what we usually attribute to them. ;-) If DW was already going
to be there for Obfuscate, what possible reason is there to give CW
also to Obfuscate? It is the purest form of wallpaper, because there
is another card, at the same rarity level, which is always and
in every case better than it.

As for the rest of the issue, I feel that making CW disciplineless is
pretty unlikely to unbalance the game (or weapons, or weapon usage) to
as great a degree as the sudden barrage of devil's advocates are suggesting.
As someone pointed out already, there are rather a number of weapon
hosers available in several cardsets, which get (as far as I know)
basically zero play right now, because weapons are inherently not all
that effective, part of which is because you do have to take the
equip action unless you have the Obfuscate for Disguised Weapon. Allowing
everyone to get to skip equip actions with CW would make equip actions
(for weapons; other equipment still (naturally) has to be equipped) less
common, certainly, but I don't think that's really such a terrible thing.

I'm not rabidly in favor of changing CW over to disciplineless, because
there are so many wallpaper cards in Jyhad/VTES that I can't really
condone 'officially' changing them all to make them useful (especially
when we still haven't changed the cards that are over-useful to bring
*them* in line). But I think the arguments against changing CW are
pretty weak.

Josh

I see that, though I frankly do not understand the concern.

> As a

Sometimes it seems as though the opponents of this move imagine that
turning CW to disciplineless would turn all weapons into Zip Guns,
such that the option to block is completely removed. I cannot help
wondering if you have ever played a Nossie or Malkavian weapon deck. If
you do, you will discover that 1) 8 weapons + 8 DWs take up alot of deck
space, 2) The weapons better be grenades and wooden stakes mostly, or
you're going to be losing alot of pool, 3) Only one of them is going to be
an Ivory Bow, since you don't want to contest yourself, 4) odds are good
that you are either going to get weapon hand-jam or DW handjam--weapon
handjam can be solved with equip actions, whereas DW handjam forces you to
discard DWs, possibly forcing you to take equip actions later in the game.

I cannot help wondering if you have ever actually tried to construct and
play a disguised weapon deck? If you had, I do not think you would regard
it as so scary.

> What you call "wasted time", I see as a necessary
> risk element that the equipping minion has to take.

Why you see it that way is completely beyond me. Did it ever occur to you
that this Arms Dealer you have Bum's Rushed might *already* have posessed
a handgun or two before he was even brought into play? He *is* an Arms
Dealer, after all. Maybe it was there all the time, but you just didn't
know about it. What's so amazing about a Brujah Weenie having a concealed
handgun or two, or any of the Brujah allies. Without CW, all the Brujah
Allies are pointless. If you get into a combat with a Loyal Street Gang,
do you really have any right to be surprised if one of them has a cheap
handgun, or a Meat Cleaver he stole from his mom, or some Brass Knuckles?
If you get into a fight with a Muddled Vampire Hunter, do you really
have any right to be surprised if he just happens to have a Wooden Stake?
You seem to feel you should have had the opportunity to block. Why, for
God's sake? Maybe Muddles just pulled a stick off the tree and sharpened
it while the sun was blazing high above him. How are your vampires gonna
block that?

And it it is easy for allies to have weapons you don't know about, why not
vampires, even weenie vampires. A Brujah might pick up a weapon or two
from his victems on a night out hunting, and if the weapon is small and
easily carried, why should anyone know about it but him?

If your Renegade Garou attacks Angel (or some other weenie), and then gets
blown away by a sawed-off shotgun, does the Garou's Methuselah really
have the right to whine and complain, saying "I should have known angel
had a sawed off shotgun, and should have had a chance to block her."
Really? Why should you have known? Why should you necessarily have had a
chance to block her getting it? She may well have been keeping it hidden
so you did not know it was there, and as far as blocking it, she could
have picked one up from any of a hundred punk victems during the last 50
years or so of her undead existence.

The Methuselah still has to pay the cost of the weapon, and that in itself
is sufficient to prevent the "unblockable" equip action from being
seriously abusive.

> If you want to

A difficult (5 card) combo to pull off, and nothing the Nossies cannot do

spite of their access to a superior form of CW (DW). It helps, but it
doesn't help *that* much.

But why should the Brujah go to the trouble of getting obfuscate just so
they have a few weapons that no-one had a chance to block? They gain
blood from the Warzone Hunting Ground without having to take actions, so
why shouldn't they gain some weapons in the process from the punks they
drain? They have arms dealers and street gangs for allies. Why on earth
should the Justicar of the Brujah need some out-of-clan discipline just so
he can get some brass knuckles.

>

No, it merely eliminates the opportunity to block most equip weapon

> and allows for weapons to be brought out at

YES!! And this is a GOOD thing!

> This advantage

nononononono....Obfuscate merely allows you to hide bigger weapons. If

wants to hide some stuff in his coat so Dracula does not know exactly what

There are actually a great many disciplined cards for which the inferior

version. Consider:

NO BETTER

> I might be swayed in this argument if
> there were additional limiting provisions (non-unique weapons, only
> and/or lower damage/cost thresholds)

I don't think these are necessary. I do have some sympathy with the idea
of a non-unique weapon limitation, but only if one were to design a new
card for a new set (which is not likely). If we errata CW we should keep
the errata short and simple.

> >>I take most of these weapons and throw them in the Horrid

>

Every drop. Still, my Nossies have an option that others don't.

> >>CW doesn't sufficiently limit exactly what weapons
> >>it allows minions without Obf to get without risk of a blocked action.
>
> >I would have preferred that Unique Weapons be excluded, but this because I
> >am just a little jealous of my Nossies' privileges, not because I think
> >it makes Weapon-based combat too powerful.
>
> Allowing any minion to pull out an Ivory Bow with impunity doesn't
> make weapon based combat too powerful?!? Sure.

You seem to pick particularly on Ivory Bow. Now, I understand that,
compared to other weapons, Ivory Bow is a rather overpowered or
underpriced card. Normally, the fact that it is unique should be enough
to compensate for the fact that it is slightly more powerful than other
cards of the same price, but Ivory Bow is a little more powerful even than
that. Part of the problem is the new Agro Damage rules, which allows an
Ivory Bow to do almost equivalent to what a 2R agro damage weapon would
have done under the old rules. Even under the old rules, however, Ivory
Bow compares rather well to Sengir Dagger, which costs 2 pool and cannot
be used at range. I would say that the problem here, however, is not that
CW as disciplineless is too powerful, but rather that Ivory Bow is
slightly overpowered/underpriced (stricly compared to other weapons),
particularly with the revised agro damage rules.

But how abusive is Ivory Bow/CW, really? Compare it to that other 2-card
combo: Zip Gun/DBR. The latter grants you a maneuver to long range,
gives you 2 agg +1 damage, and costs no pool. You can't really build a
deck around Ivory Bow/CW, because Ivory Bow is unique. You have the
advantage that you can keep it in play as a permanent (unlike Zip
Gun/DBR), but are lost if it gets contested, stolen, or burned. Even
under the new agro rules, Ivory Bow is not so deadly in a world where
anyone can get agro damage for the cost of a protean discipline card, or
ranged agro damage with thaumaturgy. Ivory Bow, in addition, can never do
more than 1 agg, can be dodged, prevented, IG'd or DOTB's into
uselessness, stolen or destroyed with first strike, etc. Without a
manuever to long range, anyone with an Ivory Bow stands a good risk of
being torporized (with less blood remaining) along with his opponent.

I sympathize somewhat with your reservations regarding Ivory Bow. If I
were to design a similar card for a future set, if might have included a
no-unique-weapons rule. However, no new sets are anticipated, and I think
that a disciplineless CW would enhance the game greatly. The benefits far
outweight the potential for Ivory Bow abuse, though the recommended fix
will certainly result in Ivory Bow being contested with greater frequency.

> >>Sorry, but I _like_ the fact that there's at least a shot of blocking
> >>someone from equipping with the Ivory Bow, even if its just a wistful
> >>thought, as my Nosferatu look on in abject horror ;-) That
> >>opportunity to block is gone once CW is disciplineless.
>
> >To a large extent it is, but why should it not be this way? Are you
> >really afraid that weapon-based combat will become TOO powerful? The
> >difficulty and time getting weapons into play is one of the major reasons
> >(along with their cost) they are not played at all.
>
> I object to eliminating the rules-provided, tried and true method of
> denying a minion equipment... to block.

To you also object to the way Hunting Grounds cards prevent you from
blocking minions from gaining a blood from their mortal victims?

> It's the best way to pre-empt
> any action based stategy by any opponent, and it would be summarily
> denied by this suggested correction.

I don't know what you mean by "summarily". I am not suggesting errata to
turn all weapons into combat cards ala Zip Gun. I don't see at all why
equip actions should necessarily be blockable.

> As for weapons "not being played
> at all" that's a function of your meta-game, definitely _not_ so in
> mine...

From what you've described of your metagame, it sounds like the more
expensive weapons are never used, and others rarely. When they are used,
they are used by weenies, because for weenies, the cost of an equip action
is rather less than for big vampires. Let me ask, though, how often do
your combat decks include Fast Hands or Shattering Blow, or Canine Horde?

> >> This would also speed up weenie gun decks, as there is no delay for
> >>the equip action. Another negative, IMHO.
>
> >The only thing wrong with Weenie Gun decks, that I can see, is Zip
> >Gun/DBR, but that is a separate issue. A disciplineless CW has not a
> >chance to be nearly as abusive as that combo.
>
> Sure it does... it just lets you DBR with any gun within the context
> of combat, without needing to equip first.

Not at all. Zip Gun/DBR is a 2 card combo that grants me a maneuver,
gives me one damage, and inflicts 2 agro +1 damage on my opponent.

Compare: CW + Saturday Night Special + DBR is a 3-card combo that grants
me a maneuver, costs 1 pool, and inflicts 2 agro +1 damage on my opponent.
The need for 3 cards and the 1 pool cost more than make up for the lack of
the 1 damage.

The only other one I'd consider playing would be: CW + Sawed off Shotgun
+ DBR. Another 3 card combo that inflicts 2 agro +3 damage for the cost
of 2 pool and lacks the manuever.

If this was really so great, you's see the Malkavians play it alot. Have
you really seen it that often?

[snip lots of weapon hosers]

> >With judicious use of the above cards, you really should be able to deal
> >with weapon-based combat if it becomes a persistant nuisance.
>
> >Note that allies are immune to the last 2 effects, an important boost for
> >them as DOTB is one of the most deadly and reliable of all weapon hosers.
> >Allies need the boost that CW will give them.
>
> >I did not include the expansion cards, which include some handy equipment
> >hosers as well. Fractured Armament for one.
>
> All of these options were available before, but I'm interested in
> preserving one more;
>
> Block the equip action.

> All blocking requires a source of intercept (in the case of
> equipping), and all the other stuff listed above is just gravy. I'd
> like to point out that with CW disciplineless, you'd be forcing
> players to include the esoteric suggestions above, instead of just
> blocking., like they could before.

As I have argued already, I see no reason whatsoever that a vampire who
bums rushes some Street Gang should have had the opportunity to block
their chance to have some equipment. If you go after a street gang (or
anybody) you should take into account the possibility that they might have
some weapons that you don't know about. If you are a powerful vampire,
and you go out in public without having the means to deal with something
as simple and commonplace as a Saturday Night Special or a Pointy Stick,
then you deserve to be sent into torpor.

And I do not care how much intercept your vampires have. This will not
necessarily be enough to prevent all your fellow kindred and their mortal
allies from happening across some common handguns or pointy sticks in the
course of their day to day existence and putting them in their pockets
while you're not looking. You should not necessarily be able to block them
from doing so any more than you can block them from gaining blood from a
hunting ground, or block Grendel from letting you look at the top card of
your crypt.

It is quite possible that they had this stuff when they entered the game,
and you just didn't know about it until you attacked them. In Jyhad, alot
of stuff enters the game without a chance to block it, and there is
nothing wrong with this unless it is too powerful. In this case, it is
not.

> Specialized weapon hosers aren't wallpaper merely because weapons
> aren't heavily played, they're just plain limited in scope.

Perhaps, but you only need one Peace Treaty in a vote deck. In a combat
deck, DOTB and IG are perfectly valuable even if their are no opposing
weapons.

> Defense
> provisions should be more diverse in order to be included in a good
> deck strategy. Again, I dispute your claim that weapons are used so
> little... That is a result of your meta-game. While not problematic
> in mine either, it is balanced mostly because there is an opportunity
> to pre-empt the strategy of cheap weapons fast on small minions by
> blocking the equip action...

Actually, CW is less of an advantage for Weenies than it is for Big
Vampires. Because you can afford alot of weenies, the actions come
cheeply, and you save less by having CW to take up deck space and
potentialy jam your hand. When I play my Lucretia deck, I use weenies to
help Lucretia equip -- they gather the stuff, and then Lucretia transfers
multiple items to herself in a single action. The DW cards in the deck
are for Lucretia to equip with weapons in combat.

> >>Moot, really. So does Army of Rats.
>
> >The point is not conclusive, but it does support the position of the
> >card's original intent.
>
> Rebutted as well by my theory of a last minute change. The cards were
> already at the printers, and all that could be done was to add a
> discipline, you couldn't even remove it without needing a redo of the
> sheet layout...

That does not "rebut" the position of the cards original intent. It
*concedes* the point. I never claimed to know why the card was changed,
or why they chose not to issue errata.

I do understand that the cards original intent is not the main or the most
important issue. The issue is whether errata to this card would benefit
the game. Though I did take time to point out the cards original intent,
I have advocated errata only on the basis of the latter issue, and even
took issue with Jason for advocating it exclusively on the basis of the
former.

I think we can agree that the original intent of the card was to be
disciplineless; that we do not know if it was changed intentionally or by
accident; and that it should not be changed back unless such a change
would significantly benefit the game (I believe it would).

> I reject most real-world analogies as moot. My point though was that
> the Ivory Bow has power that goes beyond the pool/damage limit
> provided for by CW. So do several other weapons. Dimensional
> arguments about weapon size are just about as silly as the artwork
> argument below...

I only pointed these out to demonstrate the concept behind the cards
original intent, which is clear and obvious enough. THIS WAS NOT I REPEAT
NOT INTENDED BY MYSELF AS AN ARGUMENT IN SUPPORT OF ERRATA PER SE.

As for the power of Ivory Bow being inadequately compensated for by the
fact that it is unique...well that more an Ivory Bow problem than a
disciplineless CW problem. It is mainly a new-agro-rules problem. It's
not such a big problem either, since Ivory Bow is unique and cannot be
seriously abused.

Without CW, Ivory Bow is still just a little too good compared to other
weapons, meaning that it is played occasionally and the rest rarely or not
at all. With CW "fixed" all these weapons will be played more frequently,
even Ivory Bow, though this will be limitted to some extent by the fact
that it is unique (though I still doubt it will be contested as often as
Info Highway). But the imbalance between Ivory Bow and other weapons will
remain regardless of what we do to CW.

> >My position has always been that its effect would be a good one. If
> >weapon-based combat were to even slightly out of hand (and this is
> >EXTREMELY unlikely), then the worst that would happen is that the weapon
> >hosers might stop being wallpaper for a while. I seriously doubt that
> >this will happen. The Malkavians and the Nossies already have a superior
> >version of CW, and it has not done much to turn them into powerful combat
> >clans. Your alarmist fears are way off the wall.
>
> You overrate my fears by labeling them alarmist. But this change will
> eliminate another opportunity to block an action.

So what? Only equip with weapon actions, and it is debatable that you
should be always allowed that opportunity. Disciplineless CW adds far
more than it takes away.

> Think about what
> you ordinarily have to go through to make an action unblockable
> (fortitude, Concotion of Vitality, etc) and realize that this is the
> sort of power that you're providing to all minions on the equip with
> weapon action...

As far as weapon equipping goes, I approve of this entirely. Equipping
with a weapon does not (and should not) HAVE to be a blockable action, and
a minion attacking me should not necessarily know that I have an Ivory
Bow, any more than you should necessarily know that I have pack of dogs
(Canine Horde) around the corner waiting to play "fetch" with your Ivory
Bow.

I strongly approve of weapons becoming an unpredictable part of combat.
Unless you have superior Auspex, or something, why should you know ahead
of time that I have a grenade in my coat.

> >The major beneficiaries of this card would be the Allies, who are almost
> >wallpaper as it is. Now if allies were to get out of hand (don't make me
> >laugh) there are plenty of things that could be done about THAT. For
> >starters, a single Cryptic Mission will get rid of Loyal Street Gang AND
> >his .44 magnum that cost his Methuselah a combined 3 pool, and their is
> >certainly more than one way to skin THAT cat.
>
> That Cryptic Mission makes it foolish to equip the LSG with a costly
> weapon in the first place, regardless of CW discipline status.

Not necessarily foolish, but risky. I've had some fun with Ally Equip
decks, and I don't care who calls me foolish for doing so. I've never won
with them, (though I have come close) and I think that CW would make such
decks just a little more viable.

du...@newton.ruph.cornell.edu (Joshua Duffin) wrote:

>Richard D. Zopf (guenh...@mindspring.com) wrote:

>: sirt...@aol.com (SirTemple) wrote:

>: >I think this is everyone who voted thus far.
>: >It is 15-0 for making Concealed Weapon discaplineless.

>: "Why not play Devil's Advocate?" I thought, and dive right in. I'll

>Hmmm. Well, you make some reasonable points here, but I have to take

>issue with at least one of them: You suggest that the designers knowingly
>changed CW to Obfuscate, so as to keep it from being disciplineless and
>screwing up the game. But that implies stupidity on their part even
>beyond what we usually attribute to them. ;-) If DW was already going
>to be there for Obfuscate, what possible reason is there to give CW
>also to Obfuscate? It is the purest form of wallpaper, because there
>is another card, at the same rarity level, which is always and

I could only conjecture as to why they put it in Obf, other than the
similar card there already meant it would at the very least be a zero
impact change. If they felt so strongly when Jyhad was printed that
weapons wer going to be a strong part of the game, they might have
felt that erring on the conservative side was best.

>As for the rest of the issue, I feel that making CW disciplineless is
>pretty unlikely to unbalance the game (or weapons, or weapon usage) to
>as great a degree as the sudden barrage of devil's advocates are suggesting.

I'm flattered to be labeled a "...sudden barrage of devil's
advocates..." And to clarify, "unbalance" was never a term I used.
This isn't a RTI/TB/Mind Rape grade discussion we're having here.
Making CW disiplineless wouldn't be "unbalancing". It would, however,
mean that the equip action would likely be obsoleted. I'm simply
taking issue with the subsequent likely elimination of a simple block
action as a method for denying equipment to my opponent, as would be
the case with most weapons after this proposed errata to CW.

>As someone pointed out already, there are rather a number of weapon
>hosers available in several cardsets, which get (as far as I know)
>basically zero play right now, because weapons are inherently not all
>that effective, part of which is because you do have to take the
>equip action unless you have the Obfuscate for Disguised Weapon. Allowing
>everyone to get to skip equip actions with CW would make equip actions
>(for weapons; other equipment still (naturally) has to be equipped) less
>common, certainly, but I don't think that's really such a terrible thing.

Weapon hoser cards are reactionary, not pre-emptive. The best
defensive strategies fall into the latter category, and not the
former. Blocking is a pre-emptive methodology given to (nearly) all
minions, and shouldn't be made obsolete in the case of weaponry. If
the suggested errata wer to be instated, the number and quality of
weapons that the CW cost/damage restriction applies to isn't nearly
high enough.

>I'm not rabidly in favor of changing CW over to disciplineless, because
>there are so many wallpaper cards in Jyhad/VTES that I can't really
>condone 'officially' changing them all to make them useful (especially
>when we still haven't changed the cards that are over-useful to bring
>*them* in line). But I think the arguments against changing CW are
>pretty weak.

I think the idea that there are other cards to be changed before this
is addressed is a good one... There's so much more that deserves
attention before this.

That must be from my Pulling your Strings ;-)

I feel like I am one of the "Twelve Angry Men", with R.David Zopf as the Henry
Fonda (or Jack Lemmon - depending on which version) character. I am starting to
fall into his way of thinking that if CW was left as it was, it would make the
equip action obsolete. Instead of making only making it disciplineless (which
is no doubt easier), what about the following fix (this copied from the WOTC
page and then altered):

Card Title: Concealed Weapon
Blood/Pool: n/a
Clan/Discip.: n/a
Card Type: Action Modifier
+1 stealth. This can only be used by a minion attempting to equip with a
weapon.
Pay weapon's equip cost from blood pool, as normal. The weapon cannot
cost more than 2 pool or do more than 4 damage.
Artist: Jeff Menges
Rarity: Common 3

Good things about this suggestion: saves the card from wallpaper, gives
weapons and allies some more guts in the game.
Bad things: It pretty much changes the entire card except the name, and is
not really errata - the changes are too sweeping.

I haven't changed my vote to a nay yet, but R. David is starting to sway me...

Chris

In article <ELaiaHAU...@obeah.demon.co.uk>, James Coupe wrote:
>
>I would have to sort of agree here.

I think you overestimate the potential of CW to achieve this end. The

The Brujah are perfectly capable of making combat decks without weapons,
due to the combo of potence and protean. Enhancing weapon-based combat
gives them other equally viable advantages. They can put weapon-based
combat cards in at the expense of leaving other combat cards out.
Including weapon-based combat does not make them more powerful, merely
more variable and unpredictable. The toreador are not known as a combat
clan, and if they were enabled to become one as a result of a CW fix this
would IMO be no trajedy.

>- their major problem in
>weapon decks is the lack of stealth to get them out - you'd have to give
>them Obfuscate, or get them out under stealth and Heidelberg them or
>smoething - or just hope and prey no-one has intercept, and intercept
>locations or fairly common.
>
>As said, you'd hardly ever equip a weapon again!

If you were willing to devote 20% of your deck to weapons and CW cards
then the obligation to equip with actions would be minimized (though not
necessarily eliminated). I see no problem with this, especially since Zip
Gun shows precedent as an weapon card that doubles as a combat card,
setting as strong precedent for the concept (as does DW of course).

>Malkavians have very little combat defence - Auspex has a dodge or two,
>and a little damage prevention. Dominate is very poor (besides the
>broken TB). Obfuscate lets them have that surprise value - at a price,
>the cost of a weapon.

Obfuscate still gives them the advantage of being able to equip when
choosing a strike, not at all insignificant. Even the inferior version of
CW grants them the abililty to equip with a Bomb, which CW cannot do, and
this is a good as a defensive (though not offensive) move. Malkavians are
also the premier stealth bleeders, and it is not necessarily a bad thing
that they are not the best in combat.

>It's not likely to be great because a pure combat
>deck likely has damage prevention cards, or flak jackets etc. But it is
>there, for security.

It's still there for them, and gives them greater options.

>Assamites can have fun with it, Obfuscate Celerity being very useful.
>They are, to my mind, underpowered though,

Primarily because there are so few of them. They might well be quite
powerful if they had 23 vampires in the clan, and 20 odd cards in their
primary discipline.

>so it's not as bad as the
>Brujah and Toreador - they can vote, bleed and fight. The Assamites can
>only do the last one and, perhaps, bleed a little. So I come in, drop
>in my .44 Magnum and blast away like merry hell - a good thing that only
>their clan has GOOD access to (City Gangrel also in parts).

>by very experienced Nosferatu players, their disciplines just don't mesh
>too easily. Disguised Weapon lets them drop in a fwe weapons now and
>then to mean that you don't have to go for high capacity Nossies with
>fortitude or whatever.

This is the point I must really take issue with. I do not think the
Nossies were ever intended to be the primary weapon-using combat clan, nor
do I believe they would suffer in the sort of weapon-rich environment that
might be encouraged by a disciplineless CW. A weapon-rich combat
environment would BENEFIT the Nossies because they are the premier WEAPON
HOSERS extraordinaire. With both Animalism and Potence, they have access
to both Immortal Grapple and Drawing out the Beast: the two most
important weapon-hosers since they are useful even if your opponent does
not use weapons. They can cancel opponent's manuevers, and have access to
both Canine Horde and Shattering Blow. Fast Hands is just about the only
weapon hoser they cannot use. This more than compensates for any
exclusive equiping privileges they would lose if CW became disciplineless.
The Nossies are my favoritle clan by far (I play them more than 50% of the
time), yet I do not by any means fear that a "fixed" CW would hurt them.

>Basically, I don't care about the INTENT of the card. We've already
>proven that the card probably was meant to be disciplineless.
>Personally, I don't agree that, even though it was planned to be, that
>it SHOULD be.

I do agree on this point, and I have tried not to argue for its "fixing"
on the basis of its intent. The fact that the fix seems to "fit", is only
an added bonus, from my point of view.

>Personally, I believe that the ability to drop weapons
>into a game should be restricted to Obfuscate - handing it out willy
>nilly just isn't right.

I don't agree here. The ability to "drop weapons into a game" was build
into the game. Zip Gun was actually designed as a combat card with this
concept in mind.

>AND even if the RT do say "Yeah, alright, you can have it as
>disciplineless, we were wrong" or something, what does this mean in real
>life, as opposed to JOL? Well, any player who is new to the game or who
>has difficulty accessing Jyhad cards (I'll say for myself that it's now
>quite difficult in Britain simply because of the fact that most stores
>can't order them anymore and that places in America are saying "Yeah,
>only 5 dollars a box - just order 75 billion of the things.") Anyone
>who hasn't been playing the game from the start or who doesn't frequent
>the sealed booster tournaments or who is edgy or finds it difficult to
>buy cards from places such as the Edgeman is at disadvantage. They
>don't have this wonder card which will let them do wonders for weapons -
>no, they still have shitty old Disguised Weapon. And you want to do
>that? You want to put new players to the game at a serious
>DISADVANTAGE?

You have a point here, but not much of one. It is a common card from the
original set. The new player will have a much easier time getting it than
a rare card from any set, especially a new one. People with Protected
Resources have an advantage as well.

If a new expansion ever comes out, a corrected CW could easily be
reprinted. Until then CW, as a common card from an underpriced set, is
likely to be more readily available than a great many other valuable
cards from the newer sets.

>Most of the cards removed from Jyhad were done so because
>they were dross so no player is at a disadvantage there if they only own
>V:TES. Now you want to say "Yeah, well, being as you're new, we're
>playing with some kick ass old cards. Oh, and by the way, they don't
>sell them anymore at Local Gaming Store X. <evil laugh>" Just doesn't
>seem right to me.

Well, they also "fixed" Rotschreck to make it more as a defensive card,
and it is now one of the few defenses against TB available. I guess that
does not make it right. Still they did not remove the discontinued cards
from the game. Movement of the Slow Body is still used to great effect in
Gangrel Freaky Bleed Gangrel Decks.

That does not necessarily make it right. But why should it bother their
conscience? These are the same guys that like to put alot of overpowered
cards in newer sets so that the old cards from the old sets become
wallpaper, so that they sell alot of new cards and betray those customers
taht invested so much in the older set. Why would a move in the opposite
direction be immoral?

Hmmm...the majority of the arguement seems to revolve around blocking
and its relative importance. Some rambling notes:

1. CW does take up a card slot. So I look at my deck and decide which
cards come out so that CW goes in. It seems that I would be best off
taking my slots out of existing weapon slots; as it is a 90 card deck
I would deem 4-6 CW's as being effective. Playing a weapon based deck
I probably have 8-12 slots for equipment (15 if I am going nuts). So
2-3 of the cards come out of my weapons and 2-3 out of other cards.

After a little review....it seems that the laws of deck construction
even this part out pretty good. I have fewer weapons and no guarantee
that I will have both CW and a weapon in my hand at the same time,
also if I have to equip to avoid hand jams, fewer blocks are required by

my opponent to cripple my weapons supply. Also, how much does it hurt
detract 2-3 cards from the rest of my deck? - I may need that intercept
or stealth quite badly (which is why the zip gun is so popular in
intercept decks). Sadly, CW creates as many problems as it solves.
Re-evaluating my deck once more I find that 4 CW's is probably the
most I can put in without doing serious harm to another facet of my
deck design - no matter how robust it is.

So, what does it add to the game? A couple of CW's provides a nasty
surprise every now and then and keeps your opponents a little more
honest....just a little. This hardly detracts from the blocking
aspect of the game and provides the bonus of spicing things up a
little.

2. Many of the clans that would make best use of this have little
or no stealth capabilities (Toreador, Tzimisce, Ravnos, Brujah, and
Gangrel to name a few). This makes the equipping action for them
ridiculously easy to block - too easy - which is why successful weapon
decks are more than a rarity. CW (given the deck construction trade
offs mentioned above) merely gives the weapon deck a slightly better
shot at success. No sin in my eyes.

I still vote yes.

Though I may prefer it to be disciplineless and cost 1 pool. (1 blood
if you make the card for vampires only)

(Snipped all from various persons)

We play Concealed Weapon as a skill-less card for over a year now - and
weapons STILL not show up in masses or become predominant or abusive.

This is perhaps because most abusive weapons are unique, and nearly all
weapons cost pool you normally want to spend elsewhere to support your
strategy. Most people don't want to play a weapon based combat deck
regulary because discipline driven decks are faster and equally
effective, if not even more.

There are some weapons which may be used abusively:

Zip Gun (may be abusive with various Ammo Cards, especially DBR)
Wooden Stake (as the poor man's non-unique Senguir Dagger)

But when weapons show up more regulary, a MINOR change in the metagame
prevents weapons / equipment to become too powerful.

1st: Drawing out the Beast and Immortal Grapple are staple cards for
combat decks anyway and deny your opponent the use of his weapons /
equipment

2nd: The combat avoidance strategy with Dodge and S:CE renders weapons
nearly useless

3rd: Anti-Equipment cards would show up a little bit more, and since it
is so much easier to destroy equipment than to equip with it (especially

considering card cost) the mere existence of few anti-equipment cards
will deter others to overly use stuff

4th: Equipment decks usually are slow compared to discipline-orientated
ones, and they tend to jam your hand often (and this is no fun!).

5th: You only have a limited supply of card slots. When you use them up
for weapons or other permanents, you cannot use them for aggressive
actions or modifiers or any cards that support your strategy. Using CW
doubles the card space you need for your weapons.

To finish: We found that weapons may be a valuable supply of your deck -

but most vampires could easily deal with this threat with minimum
effort.

Minions which need weapons the most are allies, because they don't have
access to disciplines (with some exceptions). They need the additional
punch weapons can offer to them, and since most allies are mortal, they
can BUY this equipment during the daylight hours when (nearly) all
vampires are asleep. So vampires should (normally) not be able to block
such actions themselves from the point of logic. CW is a card which
enables vampires / minions to REVEAL the weapons they EQUIPPED with in
secret / in the daylight / with the help of mortals they seduced /
dominated to do their bidding.

The restriction of CW does limit the weapons revealed with it to
physically disguisable equipment, perhaps under a trenchcoat (Take a
look at Highlander...)

When you actually need supernatural powers to disguise equipment because

it is so bulky, you need DW anyway.

To make CW officially disciplineless would add to the game, and in my
experience doesn't change much. Yes. You may perhaps not like that your
opponent gets a 44er out of his trench, but that's life. When you think
that you need supernatural powers to hide a "Senguir" Dagger, get a
knife out of your kitchen, put it inside your jacket and watch yourself
in a mirror. You will be surprised that even you, a mere mortal, have
this "inferior obfuscate" to use CW in reality... Why not in this card
game?

Michael Beer

I never said they were. I am merely pointing out that a disciplineless CW
does not even come near to turning all guns into Zip Guns. To achieve
that effect, you would have to make a house rule stating that all weapons
can be played as combat cards, same as Zip Gun.

I agree that a CW/Saturday-Night-Special combo is significantly more
powerful than Zip Gun by itself. And that is precisely as it should be.
After all, the first effect is achieved by playing 2 cards and the second
by playing only one.

In an game environment where card values are approximately equal, one
would expect that playing 2 cards would be approximately twice as
effective as playing only one. I don't think, however, that the CW/S-N-S
combo even gets close to being twice as effective as the single card
effect of Zip Gun -- not after you factor in the many disadvantages.

jam inherent in the fact that CW is a card that REQUIRES a combo.

Not fair. You were supposed to make allowances for inebriation.

strategy, you must put a weapon/CW mix in your deck consisting of a total

out of your deck instead -- combat cards that are not hosed by DOTB and
others.

A brujah weapon/cw deck could be awesome in the right circumstances, but
so could other types of brujah combat decks, which have the advantage of
not costing you pool when you play combat cards.

No doubt. Even with CW, however, people will not shriek in fear when the
Toreador appear. Perhaps we would see the Toreador doing "pretty well in

doubt) then a small shift in the metagame to anti-weapon strategies would

[snip]

>>Gun shows precedent as an weapon card that doubles as a combat card,

>You get the 1R and maneuver, of course, but you also take damage every
>time you use it. You'll get through a lot of damage prevention that
>way, or take a fair bit of damage.

Zip Gun is not all that limitted when you consider its advantages. Even
if Zip Gun was a normal weapon card, and not a combat card, one could
still argue that it was balanced compared to Saturday Night Special.
Advantage that it costs 1 less pool is arguably balanced by the fact that
it does one damage each combat to the bearer.

However, when you add in the advantage of playing it as a combat card,
with not action requirement and no opportunity to block, then it becomes
clear that Zip Gun easily outweighs Saturday Night Special in its
advantages.

Allowing S-N-S to be used with CW helps even the odds a little. Remember
you still cannot equip as easily as you can with a Zip Gun, because a
combo is required.

>limited, less functional version of the card is available
>disciplineless. The thing is, with Disguised Weapon, we already have

The above statement is wrong. Zip Gun is definitely NOT more limited than

Zip Gun is definitely superior and far more versatile and effective.

Here's a way of looking at it. Flak Jacket costs 1 pool and one minion
action, and saves one damage per combat. Zip Gun, when compared to
Saturday Night Special, saves one pool and one minion action, and costs 1
damage per combat. Thus if we use Flak Jacket as a measure of appropriate
cost vs. benefit, Zip Gun appears balanced compared to Saturday Night
Special.

On second thought, however, the balance begins to fade with the following
consideration: After you play Zip Gun, you only take the damage when you
choose to use the gun, so the damage is only applied when you feel the
cost is appropriate. You can play the Zip Gun without fear, knowing that
if you do not want to take the damage, you do not have to use the gun.
With Saturday Night Special (or Flak Jacket), you have no such guarantee
that your costs will be compensated for.

And a third thought: Flak Jackets are not extremely useful or valuable.
Most players feel, on average, that the disadvantages tend to slightly
outweigh the advantages. If so, it follows that for Zip Gun, the
advantages may outweigh the disadvantages.

On balance, then, Zip Gun is a more valuable card than Saturday Night
Special.

Comparing Zip Gun to a *successful* CW/S-N-S Combo, the combo comes out
slightly on top. Zip one saves one pool, but costs 1 damage per combat
(but only when you decide it is wise to use the Zip Gun). The combo is
arguably a little better, but is in no way *twice* as good.

Zip Gun's side. Perhaps it is unfair to mention the broken ZipGun/DBR,
but how about ZipGun/ManstopperRds, ZipGun/FlakJacket,

>times someone says it, Zip Gun will still not be a "more limited version
>of Disguised Weapon."

Well, being as it kind of seems I started this little wrangle, I'll try
and explain what *I* meant. Feel free to disagree of course :)

Basically, the idea I was getting at was this. Imagine that you are
playing a Brujah combat deck, right? You decide to rush me with Volker.

Example 1: You rush Rudolpho Giovanni (3/3) NEC. Looking at the deck,
you've decided that he probably can't defend himself very well. I,
though, when I was making the deck knew that and decided to put a little
bit of combat defence in. I wanted a way to get weapons out in combat
without having to waste an action on it. I didn't have much Obfuscate
in the deck at all (maybe only one or two vampires) so I decided to put
a Zip Gun in the deck. Okay, I'll end up taking a bit of damage with it
but I get a pretty nice gun all the same and don't have to equip it.
It's probably not going to be enough to kill you but at least I'll be
able to put up some semblance of a fight.

Example 2: You rush Murat (7/7) OBF POT ser. Well, the main point of
the deck was a bit of Obfuscate Serpentis for corrupting people with
things like Temptation and Form of Corruption, things like that. Murat
was in there for a bit of voting skill if needed. Having seen the deck,
you think it should be fairly easy to make it roll over and die.
Obviously, when constructing the deck, I took that into account and
decided to put a few weapons in that I didn't have to get with an
action. Well, I decided that I should use Disguised Weapon instead of
Zip Gun. It takes a few more cards and requires two cards in my hand,
but this way I can get some more powerful cards out. Instead of simply
having to pop at you with a poxy one damage, I can get aggravated hand
damage, lots of hand damage (weapon damage), aggravated ranged damage,
guns, even the ability to prevent damage (Talbot's).

Now you, not being stupid, in both cases thought "Well, there is a
possibility that he can get a weapon out and hit me back." In the first
case, the only weapon possible was Zip Gun. You didn't really care
about that because it couldn't do enough damage to stop you. If it was
DBR-ed then at least you'd feel vindicated by falling prey to ultra-
cheese.

When rushing Murat, you realised he has far more options available to
him. He could get a weapon out when he chooses his strike - which will
be after you've declared yours. What do you do? Go to range and see if
he has guns? Stay at close to pound him good and proper and hope he
doesn't have a Sengir Dagger? Run screaming from the might of a
Flamethrower? Whatever.

And that was what *I* meant by Zip Gun being a more limited,
disciplineless version of Disguised Weapon. In both cases, you have the
opportunity to bring out a weapon to defend yourself when you previously
didn't have one. Zip Gun brings you out a little gun, fairly crappy and
you have no choice about that. Disguised Weapon can bring you out any
weapon. Yes, you have to have the two card combo but that isn't that
hard. It's just that Disguised Weapon is more flexible in that sense.
I could decide to use lots of little weapons, pretty cheap ones - things
like Brass Knuckles, Saturday Night Specials, maybe an Ivory Bow. Or I
could go for the big stuff. A few well placed Flamethrowers, Sub
Machine Guns and the like will soon put the mockers on a deck if you're
lucky. Or do I want to take the melee weapon angle? A few Bastard
Swords here or there, a Sengir Dagger and maybe even a Bang Nakh should
suitably annoy enough people. And a Melee Weapon is generally cheaper
than it's equivalent ranged weapon so what do you want to choose? If we
go back to Zip Gun, I simply don't have the flexibility to decide if I
want any different weapons. That was what *I* meant by Zip gun being
more limited. I'm not saying it isn't a good, usable card. I've seen
it used to exactly the opposite effect. I was ousted because of a Zip
Gun at Crusade: Cardiff last year (this is true - the damage sentthe
vampire to torpor, activating the fame and ousting me). The only thing
I'm saying is that since both Disguised Weapon and Zip Gun allow you to
bring out weapons in combat, it makes sense to have some comparison
running between the two and for my money, the added flexibility of
Disguised Weapon meant that it, IMHO, was generally more powerful than a
Zip Gun.

--

When I lived in Edmonton, we had CW disciplineless for several months
before I ended up going to Yellowknife. We made it generic for all of
the reasons you've mentioned and a few more.

After a few decks were made, played, tuned, played again, tuned some
more, played again, retired. We decided that it really made no huge
differences in the game and was thus worth keeping as a house rule.
It was really most useful to the intercept decks (specifically Toreador
and Tor-anti) which is interesting as many posts in this thread have
noted that a disciplinless CW hurts the blocking aspect of the game.

It has always seemed sad to me that the blocking clans, clans with
auspex as a primary disc., (Tor, Tor-anti, Ven-anti, Tzi, Tre, and
Malk) all have trouble with combat. The Malks can use DW, so a CW
discussion doesn't apply to them. The other clans though can be
considered though, with Toreador serving as the poster boy.

Though celerity is also a major part of the clan, celerity in and
of itself (most importantly, by itself)is inadequate as a combat
discipline. To deal with the opponents S:CE you need a good supply
of Psyche's, to deal with the combat clans IG's you need a lot
of maneuvers....either way you are using a lot of card slots up
and you aren't doing anyone any damage yet. Throw in the intercept
you need, and all of a sudden....not many cards left to build up
that second combat discipline you need so badly (pot, pro, etc.).

That leaves weapons, which is why the cheesy Intercept/Zip-gun/
DBR decks live. Why zip-guns?, I ask the rhetorical question -
because Toreador have no stealth to speak of. Any little +1
intercept allows your opponent to deny your minions the weapons
they need so badly, the weapons that they are much less effective
without (neutered almost). So zip-guns rule.

I could go on and on here, but my soapbox is wearing out. We found
that CW as a generic combat card allowed one to build more (marginally)
competitive intercept/weapon decks. None of these decks ever won a
game, and only twice did it come close. This holds true for all of
the weapon decks that were built to take advantage of our CW
house rule.

Thanks,
Jaysen

Well, I'm glad you don't see it as a game balance issue, since that
position is hardly defensible.

Your "principle" is still confusing to me. What rule states that one must
have an opportunity to block when permanent resources are brought into
play? The rule is that this opportunity exists only if the resources
enter play *as an action*.

Contrast unique locations that are played as equipment with unique
locations that are played as master cards. Both are permanent resources
for a methuselah's minions. In some cases you can block, whereas in some
cases you cannot. The cases where you cannot in no violate any rule about
permanent resources being blockable.

opportunity to block diablerie?

Does Heidelberg Castle contradict any principle that there should be an
opportunity to block the transfer of equipment?

Do Hunting Grounds Cards contradict any principle that there should be an
opportunity to block the gaining of blood from human prey?

Vampires are another permanent resource that come into play with no
opportunity to block. For a cost of 4 pool a Methuselah can bring
Agrippina into play, and no-one can block this. For the cost of 6 pool
and a DW/BangNakh combo, a Methuselah gains Agrippina with +2 hand damage,
with no opportunity to block. In neither case is any principle of Jyhad
violated.

Your principle is already violated with Zip Gun, as well as by the
superior card Disguised Weapon. And please don't repeat that Zip Gun is a
more limited version of Disguised Weapon. Of the two cards, only Zip Gun
has had the more unbalancing effect on the game. Disguised Weapon has
never had this effect, despite that there are plenty of obfuscate weenies
available to play it.

A disciplineless CW is inappropriate only if the effect is unbalanced.

Greetings RDZ

The problem I with your responses below, is that you seem to be
substituting the concept of "game balance" (which most of us can
understand to some degree) to an even more nebulous concept of
"appropriate limitations", which seem to have nothing to do with the
concept of game balance. Naturally, I agree that cards must have
"appropriate limitations", but only to the extent that considerations of
"game balance" determine which limitations are appropriate. You seem to
have already conceded (or at least, failed to contest) the argument that
DW and CW are not overpowered. To me, this means that such limitations as
they already posess are perfectly adequate, but here we seem to split. You
seem to be using alternate criteria for determining whether the
limitations on a disciplineless CW are appropriate, but what those
criteria are remain a complete mystery to me.

CW and DW also have numerous "non-blocking" options. Direct Intervention
immediately comes to mind as the minion-card counterpart to Sudden
Reversal (and is particularly apt since you can effectively burn 2 cards
for the price of one by using it against the weapon card), but one's
non-blocking options are hardly limitted to this. Weapons can be stolen

Incidentally, an increase in the number of weapons in play would increase

generally more powerful than non-unique ones -- the idea being that a
limitation of uniqueness compensates for additional advantages.

that it is not overpowered.

>
> All of these examples are much more limited in scope of what and when
> they apply to the interferance of the standard action based
> equivalent. Amaranth requires a vampire going to torpor, HC exchanges
> once between two minions, and HG's are clan specific. All limited in
> scope of applicability to a greater or lesser extent.

Indeed they are, (to a greater or lesser extent -- as is CW). Heidelberg
Castle is indeed "limited in scope", but these "limitations" were so
inadequate that the card was seriously overpowered, and had to be fixed by
further limitations. Even with errata, it is one of the most contested
locations in the game. If "game balance" is taken as our guide to
appropritate limitations, then the limitations on a fixed CW are clearly
more appropriate than those on HC.

CW has alot of it's own limitations compared to HC:
- Only usable on weapons (an underplayed and underpowered aspect of the
game) rather than on ANY equipment. Even some weapons are
excluded.
- Not usable with retainers
- Cannot be used to transfer blood
- Requires alot of deck space to use effectively - with high hand-jam
potential

> >Vampires are another permanent resource that come into play with no
> >opportunity to block. For a cost of 4 pool a Methuselah can bring
> >Agrippina into play, and no-one can block this. For the cost of 6 pool
> >and a DW/BangNakh combo, a Methuselah gains Agrippina with +2 hand damage,
> >with no opportunity to block. In neither case is any principle of Jyhad
> >violated.
>
> This is limited as an example to minions which cost four that have
> obfuscate. Again, limited scope...

Huh? Basil has 1 capacity. Dimple and Normal have 2 capacity. Vampires
with obfuscate come in all sizes, and this trick may be used with them
all.

Constantly repeating "limited scope" is nothing more than reciting a
mantra in lieu of real discussion. All cards are limited in scope. There
is no card called "Unlimited Scope" which says has "do anthing you want"
as it's card text. Even overpowered, broken cards like TOR3 and RTI are
limited in scope.

> >Your principle is already violated with Zip Gun, as well as by the
> >superior card Disguised Weapon. And please don't repeat that Zip Gun is a
> >more limited version of Disguised Weapon. Of the two cards, only Zip Gun
> >has had the more unbalancing effect on the game. Disguised Weapon has
> >never had this effect, despite that there are plenty of obfuscate weenies
> >available to play it.
>
> Zip Gun is unbalanced.

Only because of the DBR combo, which I agree needs to be fixed somehow.
Otherwise, it is only one of the few weapon cards which are not wallpaper
or almost wallpaper.

> It seems that it would be less of a problem,
> though, if only some fraction of the minions within the game could
> make use of it.

It would be less of a problem if the DBR combo were fixed in one of 2
ways: Either forbid ammo, or have the ammo also increase the
self-inflicted damage.

> Again, DW isn't bad because it limits the scope (by
> discipline) of who can take advantage.

[snip]

DW isn't bad, period. If it had been disciplineless from the start, the
game would still be balanced. Still, there is no danger that a
disciplineless CW will turn DW into wallpaper. Minions with Obfuscate
will always prefer DW.

> Unblockability is of the realm of Fortitude (and it's debatable
> whether it should be there) and Obfuscate. Keep it that way.

Wrongo. "Unblockability" is the realm of hundreds of combat cards and
combat strateties, most of which are arguably much more powerful and
effective than CW. CW is a combat card -- one that is easily countered.
Please compare it's effects to those of other combat cards - ones not so
easily countered, and which don't cost pool.

Maneuvers cannot be "blocked", but they can be countered. Presses cannot
be "blocked", but they can be countered. Strikes cannot be "blocked", but
they can be countered. The same is true of CW and DW. Weapon-based
combat strategies are expensive and easily hosed, a hosing that is all the
more devastating *after* you have payed all that pool for your weapons.

> Reduce the cost

Bang Nakh
